$comment: THE CHIME LEDGER — every source a chime can come from and every sink one can go to. GitHub issue #368, DECISIONS.md § D526 (the currency), § D530 (its name), § D531 (the sign-in gift), docs/38-what-the-game-is.md § 2.4. See packages/core/src/config/chimeLedger.ts for the schema and the argument. PROVENANCE, per the product owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values and the 2026-09-09 ruling on this issue in particular: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS FILE IS AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, drafted for the owner to accept, tighten or reject, and NOT ONE OF THEM IS MEASURED. The distinction that ruling asks for is drawn field by field, and here it falls entirely on one side. What is MEASURED: nothing. There is no run behind any number below, no seed set, no interval, and none is claimed — contrast data/contract-ladder.json, where the resulting miss rate of each row IS measured at a named run and the file says which half is which. What is CHOSEN: every awardChimes, every priceChimes, every grantUnits, every maxSteps, awayHours, and the ordering between them. (This sentence used to say 'every band boundary'. There was no band-boundary field in this document and there is now no band at all — see WHAT THIS FILE MAY NEVER CARRY below. A provenance line naming a field that does not exist is the same defect as a figure nobody measured, one level up.) A price ladder and an award curve are game feel; docs/38 § 2.1 says the same of the unit prices and data/price-schedule.json's own comment says it again. What WOULD measure them, and what the owner asked for on 2026-09-09, is playing the game against this table and tuning until the earn-and-spend curve is neither trivial nor a grind — the discipline docs/33 § 4.6 used for the 80 kJ bar, where 400 pinned runs bracketed the figure from both sides. That work is not done. A reader who disagrees with a number here is disagreeing with a judgement rather than correcting an error, and the lever is one field in this file rather than anything in code. WHAT THIS FILE MAY NEVER CARRY, and the parser refuses rather than the reviewer: a source earnedBy anything but 'completion' or 'gift'; a sink whose modifier kind is 'budget-units'; and a 'bands' array on any source. THE SECOND: a scenario's budget is priced BY THE SCENARIO. docs/38 § 2.1 says a budget is bought up 'in steps the scenario authors', and data/campaign.json authors exactly that — a budget.steps ladder per stage, each step carrying its own addsUnits and its own chimes, at one chime per unit — while data/scenario-survivors.json pre-simulates a survivor count against those rungs and records each rung's chimesSpent. This file shipped a 'scenario-budget-step' sink at 12 chimes for 8 units beside all of that, which is two authorities for one price: a player pays a different amount depending on which screen they are standing on, and a budget widened through the scenario's own rung could never back a posted claim. It is removed, and packages/core/src/config/chimeLedger.ts#REFUSED_MODIFIER_KINDS refuses the kind by name so it cannot come back quietly. What would let a scenario rung be bought THROUGH this ledger is a parser for the ladder that packages/server can reach; today the only one is packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.ts and invariant 6 forbids the server importing viz. THE THIRD: an award may not be banded. A 'bands' array shipped here paying 4, 6 or 10 chimes by a scenario's survivor-count band, and the server took the band VERBATIM FROM THE REQUEST BODY of the account being paid. data/scenario-survivors.json carries survivor counts and no band, nothing the earn route reads maps a count to one (data/scenario-survivor-bands.json, GitHub issue #234's drafted difficulty band, is read only by an acceptance check), and the earn route is never told which scenario was cleared. DECISIONS.md § D256: a stated mechanism is measured or withdrawn, never re-worded — so the band is withdrawn and the award is flat. § D526 clause 6 says no purchase, price, store, conversion event or supporting telemetry ships anywhere, and such a source is added only by a decision citing a measured charter S4. A price in money, a currency code, a product identifier and a bundle have no field to live in, and adding one is the change a reviewer refuses. THE SECOND HALF OF THE BOUNDARY: sources are the ledger's own vocabulary and the play surface never learns one (§ D526 clause 5). A completion is what the play surface names; a source is what the ledger calls the entry it wrote. The two are deliberately different words for that reason, and the ids below are deliberately different strings as well: a completion reads scenario-cleared and the source that pays it reads earn-scenario-clear, so a module naming one is distinguishable from a module naming the other. packages/viz/src/boundaries.test.ts asserts that no module in the viewer names a source at all, in both directions, and it derives the source ids from this file rather than transcribing them.

sources.name: A scenario cleared
sources.note: CHOSEN: 6, so two scenarios cleared buy a purse top-up. The award is FLAT, and the flatness is a decision rather than an omission: a run that clears with a suppressed mean earns exactly what a run that clears with a quotable one earns, because § D526 clause 2 forbids scaling an award by anything the run measures. It was briefly banded by the scenario's pre-simulated survivor count — permitted in principle, because a count is a property of the scenario and known before anybody plays — and the band was withdrawn because NOTHING THE EARN ROUTE READS CAN SAY WHICH BAND A SCENARIO IS IN (the one survivor band in the tree, data/scenario-survivor-bands.json, is GitHub issue #234's drafted difficulty band, and its only reader is an acceptance check). See this file's WHAT THIS FILE MAY NEVER CARRY.

sources.name: A contract day paid
sources.note: A day the contract paid for — the completed turn, not the day's figures. A missed day earns nothing and costs nothing, because § D526 clause 4 forbids anything that decays and clause 3 forbids buying relief on a miss. CHOSEN: 3, half a scenario, because a career day is a shorter turn and there are twenty of them in a week.

sources.name: A rush wave survived
sources.note: Paid per wave the run outlasted, which § D515 makes a fact about the recording rather than a statistic over it. CHOSEN: 2, the smallest award in the table, because a long rush pays several of them in one sitting.

sources.name: A gift for coming back
sources.note: § D531, in the one shape § D526 clause 7 permits: small, flat, unconditional, no compounding, no streak, and nothing lost by missing it. It has NO completion, which is the structural half of its being a gift — the play surface posts completions and can therefore not post this at all; the server writes it when a session is created and the account has been away longer than awayHours. CHOSEN: 20 hours, so a player who plays at the same time on two days meets it, and a player who plays twice in an evening does not; and 5 chimes, under one scenario cleared, so it is never the efficient way to earn. § D531 records that shipping the bonus at launch forfeits the charter S4 baseline, so NO S4 CLAIM MAY BE MADE ABOUT IT in either direction on the evidence it ships with — which is a second reason no number here is measured and none will be by watching this feature.

sinks.name: Top up this tower's purse
sinks.note: docs/38 § 2.2: chimes top up a tower's purse and may not open a slot or buy back a missed day. Slots are attention rather than money (docs/32 GD14) and a missed day is relief on a measurement (GD13 clause 5), so neither has a sink here and neither can be given one without a ruling. CHOSEN: dearer per unit than data/campaign.json's scenario rungs, which are one chime per unit, because a career purse buys works that last past the day. CHOSEN, and stated because invariant 8 now asks for it: grantUnits may be tuned over 1–100 units and maxSteps over 1–10, both bounds chosen as the room a designer plausibly needs rather than measured.

sinks.name: Start with a bigger purse
sinks.note: docs/38 § 2.3: the between-round purse a rush pays itself can be topped up before the run starts. The run then carries the modifier on its record and ranks among runs with the same modifier set (§ D526 clause 3), never among the standard ones. CHOSEN: the cheapest sink, because a rush round is the shortest turn. CHOSEN, on career-purse-top-up's own bounds and for its reason.

sinks.name: Start with the building fitted
sinks.note: docs/38 § 2.3's other rush modifier: the building starts fitted rather than as built. One step only — a building is fitted or it is not. CHOSEN as the dearest sink, because it is the one that changes the run before the first wave arrives. Its grantSchema is pinned to 0–0 and its stepSchema to 1–1, which is that sentence as a range rather than as a note: a pre-fit grants no units and happens once, and neither is a dial.
